## TabStation 2.18.1

- Fixed: the "Check for updates" button in Settings could stay on "Checking…" after the automatic check had finished.
- From 2.18.0: new setup guide, new Settings with a sidebar, in-app updates, splash screen, "Report a bug", Windows 11 style menus and many fixes. See the 2.18.0 notes for the full list.

Requires Android 10+. Shizuku is recommended. Install over the previous version; settings are kept. From 2.18.0 on, TabStation updates itself from Settings → Version & updates.

## TabStation 2.18.0

- **New setup:** a 5-step guide (Welcome, Required permissions, Full features with Shizuku, Keep running, Ready) with progress, locked steps and one-tap Shizuku setup that grants every permission at once.
- **New Settings:** a sidebar with categories (Appearance, Extra features, Dock & windows, Display & Sleep, Permissions & Shizuku, Language, Version & updates), and picture cards to choose between macOS and Windows 11.
- **In-app updates:** TabStation checks for a new version when Settings opens and can download and install it for you. Settings also shows the installed version and has a "Check for updates" button.
- **Splash screen** with an animated TabStation logo (Android 12 and later).
- **Report a bug:** in Settings → Version & updates. Your email app opens with a prefilled report: an automatic subject, device info and the TabStation log. If TabStation stops unexpectedly, it offers to send a report the next time you open it.
- **Windows mode:** right-click and long-press menus now look like Windows 11, with icons, taller rows and Windows-style highlighting.
- **Shut down** no longer says "TabStation" in the macOS and Windows menus ("Shut Down…" / "Shut down"), so it feels like part of the system.
- Fixed: the Dock didn't come back after it stopped while the desktop was still open.
- Fixed: removed or updated apps kept stale icons in the Dock.
- Fixed: a possible crash when Android restarted TabStation in the background (Android 15 and later).
- Fixed: "Stay awake while charging" stopped working when HyperOS paused charging at 80%.
- Fixed: keyboard shortcuts didn't work when Shizuku started more than about 2 minutes after TabStation.
- Fixed: Launchpad and Start could freeze briefly while app icons loaded.
- Fixed: the wallpaper image stayed in memory after shutting down.
- Fixed: the extra-features dialog wasn't translated into English.
- Security: wallpaper import only accepts images shared by other apps, the boot receiver only reacts to system events, the desktop screen can't be opened by other apps, and shell commands are harder to spoof.

Requires Android 10+. Shizuku is recommended. Install over the previous version; settings are kept. On HyperOS, allow Autostart for TabStation so it comes back after an update.

## TabStation 2.17.1

- New screenshots on the website (desktop with widgets, Edit Widgets, Control Center, Spotlight, Launchpad).
- Fixed: the menu bar could show a raw package name (e.g. after a permission dialog) instead of the app name or "TabStation".
- Fixed: apps opened from Spotlight now open after Spotlight has fully closed.
- From 2.17.0: English and Bahasa Indonesia, keyboard shortcuts, arrangeable widgets, Snap Layouts, loading screens and a clean lock screen. See the 2.17.0 notes for the full list and the shortcut table.

Requires Android 10+. Shizuku is recommended. Install over the previous version; settings are kept. On HyperOS, allow Autostart for TabStation so it comes back after an update.
